title: Atmospheric Properties for Future Earth in Each of the 10 Scenarios
transcriptionMethod: Manual transcription from the PDF table, checked against a rendered page and layout-preserving text extraction.
nullSemantics: A null transcribes the table's ellipsis: the property is not listed for that case and must not be interpreted as numeric zero.
assumptions: All cases use a 1 bar background atmosphere composed of 78% N2, 21% O2, and 1% Ar.
The published global mean temperature assumes CO2 is the dominant greenhouse gas using Equation 1 of the source.
The source model atmosphere neglects changes to average water vapor and vertical atmospheric structure.
The table values are canonical inputs for generating modeled spectra; generated spectra are derived products.
notes: Stratospheric SO2 in S1, S2, and S6 represents solar-radiation modification.
Na emission represents high-pressure sodium lighting; S1 also includes directed laser emission.
S9 and S10 have the same listed Earth atmospheric properties as preagricultural Earth R0.
PSG spectra in Figures 1 and 2 do not include the listed Na or laser emission lines.
Every column descriptor and numeric/null table cell carries an exact table row/column locator.
